findings.evidence: Statement at line 203: `∀ B : Set α, MeasurableSet B → ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto ...`; `tendsto_empiricalMeasure_apply_ae` (line 167) fixes `{B : Set α}` before the `∀ᵐ`; `tendsto_empiricalMeasure_apply_ae_forall` (line 185) requires `[Countable ι]`, and its own docstring (line 182) says interchanging the quantifiers "is not cosmetic".
findings.fix: Rephrase all six sites to the quantifier order actually proved: "for each fixed measurable set, almost surely" (and, for `_ae_forall`, "for a countable family, under one null set"). Optionally add one sentence that a.s. setwise convergence genuinely fails, since empirical measures are atomic.
findings.issue: Docstrings assert a.s. setwise convergence (`∀ᵐ ω, ∀ B`), but every theorem proves `∀ B, ∀ᵐ ω`, and the stronger claim is false: for nonatomic `ν`, take `B` = the countable set of sample points — empirical mass is 1 for all `n`, `ν B = 0`. Same overstatement at line 39-40 ("the almost-sure setwise limit"), line 161 (header "Empirical measures converge setwise, almost surely"), lines 194-195 ("recovered, almost surely and on every measurable set"), line 197 ("the pathwise limit of an explicit statistic"), and TauCeti/Probability/DeFinetti.lean:43-44 ("the almost-sure setwise limit of the empirical measures").

summary: The Lean statements and proofs are faithful: the reduction through `jointPathLaw_eq_iidMixtureLaw` to `strong_law_ae` on `Measure.infinitePi` is correct, the index shift to `empiricalMeasure` is handled, and no content is moved into hypotheses. But the documentation repeatedly claims almost-sure *setwise* convergence, which is stronger than what is proved and false in general.
